cards.heading: Agent = model + harness
cards.question: What is the 'agent = model + harness' boundary rule, and what counts as harness?
cards.answer: The model supplies raw intelligence; everything else — system prompts, tools and their descriptions, bundled infrastructure (filesystems, sandboxes, browsers), orchestration logic, and hooks/middleware for deterministic steps — is harness.

cards.heading: Design method: derive from a missing behavior
cards.question: What design method does the harness framing force when building an agent system?
cards.answer: Start from a behaviour the raw model cannot produce (e.g. durable state, code execution, knowledge past training cutoff) and derive the harness feature that supplies it.

cards.heading: Filesystem as foundational primitive
cards.question: Why is the filesystem called the foundational harness primitive?
cards.answer: It serves as workspace, context offload, cross-session persistence, and a coordination surface for multiple agents and humans working together.

cards.heading: Bash over pre-built tools
cards.question: Why do harnesses favor a general-purpose bash/code-execution tool over pre-building every specific tool?
cards.answer: Code execution is the general-purpose action, so the harness author doesn't need to anticipate and pre-build every capability in advance.

cards.heading: Context management is core harness work
cards.question: What three context-rot countermeasures does a harness typically supply?
cards.answer: Compaction when the window nears full, offloading bulky tool outputs to disk, and progressive disclosure of skill instructions.
